title: archaeology and recovery
goal: C2 Find the commit that broke it, and get back anything you lost
startWith: Use the cloned real repository from step 02 — it has enough history for these to be interesting.

newIdeas.plain: Binary search over commits, driven by a test you can run.
A local log of every position each ref held. Your undo of last resort.
Copy one commit onto another branch.

tasks.do: Bisect a bug down to one commit
tasks.why: Twelve steps over 4000 commits beats reading any of them.

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body:
git bisect start
git bisect bad                  # the current commit is broken
git bisect good <old-hash>      # this one worked
# git checks out a midpoint; test it, then say good or bad
git bisect reset

blocks.label: terminal (automated)
blocks.body:
git bisect start HEAD <old-hash>
git bisect run ./mvnw -q test -Dtest=TheFailingTest

tasks.do: Cherry-pick a fix onto a release branch

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body:
git switch release/1.x
git cherry-pick <hash>
git cherry-pick -x <hash>    # records where it came from

blocks.label: IntelliJ
blocks.body: Log → right-click a commit → Cherry-Pick. Switch to the target branch first from the branch popup.

tasks.do: Find a deleted file and restore it

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body:
git log --diff-filter=D --oneline -- path/to/gone.txt
git restore --source=<hash>~1 -- path/to/gone.txt

blocks.label: IntelliJ
blocks.body: Local History recovers files git never saw at all — the safety net under the safety net.

tasks.do: Use a worktree to look at another branch without stashing
tasks.why: A second checkout sharing one object store. Reviewing a branch stops costing you your working state.

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body:
git worktree add ../lab-review origin/some-branch
git worktree list
git worktree remove ../lab-review

proof.expect: your recent moves, including the recovery
proof.note: You located a commit by search, not by reading.

doneWhen: Losing work is no longer a category of problem you worry about.

lessons.title: Cherry-pick from the Log
lessons.teach: Switch to the target branch, then right-click the commit in the Log → Cherry-Pick. Multi-select works, and the order you pick is the order they land.
